open_points.subject: start-time validation of the run spool
open_points.text: `store` owns “private directory, no symbolic link” at `open_store`, while “the run spool's files are written, read and removed by `store_spool`, which only `store` calls”; `store_spool` offers only `remove_spool_temporaries` at start and no operation that checks every spool entry for private permissions and symbolic links
open_points.question: Which module and capability perform the required start-time scan of the entire spool for symbolic links and non-private entries, and what happens when that validation fails?
options: `store_spool` offers a start-time validate-and-clean capability called by `store.open_store`
`remove_spool_temporaries` also performs the complete spool validation
`store` scans the spool directly despite spool access being exclusive to `store_spool`
open_points.default_guess: Have `store_spool` perform complete spool validation while removing temporaries, returning a start failure to `store.open_store`.

open_points.subject: `store_spool` layout encapsulation
open_points.text: `store_spool` “Hides the spool's on-disk layout below the spool area and the run directory” but its candidate public capabilities include `spool_entry_name` and `spool_attempt_prefix`
open_points.question: Are the entry name and attempt prefix observable outputs supplied to `store`, or are they private helpers that must not be public capabilities?
options: Keep both helpers private and expose only publish, read and removal operations
Expose opaque name and prefix tokens without filesystem meaning
Expose the actual names and narrow the claim that the layout is hidden
